segments.en: Hello, English learners.
segments.zh: 各位英语学习者，大家好。

segments.en: Welcome back to another great podcast here at EnglishPod.

segments.en: And I'm Erica.

segments.en: And today we're going to be bringing you bad news.

segments.en: Actually, what we're really going to be bringing you is language to talk about bad news.

segments.en: Exactly.

segments.zh: 所以也许你必须把坏消息给你的老板，给你的父母，我不知道，某人，我们将教你如何用英语做这件事。

segments.en: Well, obviously, it's always difficult to tell somebody bad news, but in your second language, it's even harder.
segments.zh: 好吧，很明显，告诉别人坏消息总是很困难，但用你的第二语言，这就更难了。

segments.en: So we're going to try and help you today with some great phrases and vocabulary items.

segments.en: We're not going to preview anything today.
segments.zh: 我们今天不会预览任何东西。

segments.en: Let's go directly to our dialogue where we will be in a company and one of the employees is going to be giving bad news to his boss.
segments.zh: 让我们直接进入我们的对话，我们将在一家公司，其中一名员工将向他的老板提供坏消息。

segments.en: So let's listen.

segments.zh: 第一季度惨不忍睹的细节我们都听完了。埃德，说点好消息吧。

segments.en: How are things looking for us in terms of sales this month?

segments.en: Well, would you like the bad news first or the really bad news?

segments.en: What?

segments.en: Ed, don't tell me you only have bad news.
segments.zh: 埃德，不要告诉我你只有坏消息。

segments.zh: 先生，单是上个月，销售额就跌了——不，是暴跌了百分之五十。

segments.zh: 我们现在库存积压、人员过剩，利润还在快速下滑。

segments.zh: 市场不景气，存货卖不出去，员工也难以裁掉。

segments.en: If we consider redundancies, it costs us a fortune because of the new regulations governing compensation packages.
segments.zh: 若要裁员，新出台的离职补偿规定会让我们付出一大笔钱。

segments.en: It's a real mess.
segments.zh: 真是一团糟。

segments.en: You're crying out loud.
segments.zh: 真是见鬼了！

segments.en: How fast are we losing money?

segments.en: How can I put this?

segments.en: What?

segments.en: Oh, that's the really bad news.

segments.en: Our supplier suffered QC problems and, well, half of our production is faulty.

segments.en: We're going to have to recall all items sold in the last quarter and the worst part, we're going to have to shoulder this cost.
segments.zh: 上季度卖出的所有产品都得召回，更糟的是费用还得由我们承担。

segments.en: Are you joking?
segments.zh: 你在开玩笑吗？

segments.en: Get the supplier on the line now.
segments.zh: 立刻接通供应商的电话。

segments.en: They have to assume the cost of this mess.

segments.en: We tried that, sir.
segments.zh: 我们试过了，先生。

segments.en: The factory has gone under and the owner apparently has fled the country.

segments.en: Oh, we're doomed.
segments.zh: 完了，我们没救了。

segments.en: There's some really good news, though.

segments.en: Really?
segments.zh: 真的吗？

segments.en: What?

segments.en: I got offered a new job.

segments.en: All right, it sounds like a pretty tough time for this company, doesn't it?
segments.zh: 好吧，这对这家公司来说听起来很艰难，不是吗？

segments.en: But good news for the employee.

segments.en: He won't be jobless.

segments.zh: 我们需要保护环境。

segments.en: For crying out loud.

segments.en: Exactly.
segments.zh: 正是这样。

segments.en: So we have two nice sort of complimenting phrases for delivering bad news and why don't we hear them one more time in the dialogue.
segments.zh: 所以我们有两种很好的赞美短语来传递坏消息，为什么我们在对话中没有再听到一次。

segments.en: Now that we've been over the gory details of our disastrous first quarter, Ed, give us some good news.
segments.zh: 第一季度惨不忍睹的细节我们都听完了。埃德，说点好消息吧。

segments.en: How are things looking for us in terms of sales this month?
segments.zh: 本月销售情况怎么样？

segments.en: Well, would you like the bad news first or the really bad news?
segments.zh: 您想先听坏消息，还是更坏的消息？

segments.en: What?
segments.zh: 什么？

segments.en: Don't tell me you only have bad news.
segments.zh: 不要告诉我你只有坏消息。

segments.en: Well, sir, our sales have dropped.
segments.zh: 好吧，先生，我们的销售额下降了。

segments.en: No plunged 50% in the past month alone.
segments.zh: 仅在过去的一个月中，就没有暴跌 50%。

segments.en: We are currently overstocked and overstaffed and our profits are falling fast.
segments.zh: 我们现在库存积压、人员过剩，利润还在快速下滑。

segments.en: The market is in recession and we have no way of moving our inventory or getting rid of our staff.
segments.zh: 市场不景气，存货卖不出去，员工也难以裁掉。

segments.en: If we consider redundancies, it costs us a fortune because of the new regulations governing compensation packages.
segments.zh: 若要裁员，新出台的离职补偿规定会让我们付出一大笔钱。

segments.en: It's a real mess.
segments.zh: 真是一团糟。

segments.en: You're coming out loud.
segments.zh: 你大声说出来。

segments.en: How fast are we losing money?
segments.zh: 我们赔钱的速度有多快？

segments.en: How can I put this?
segments.zh: 这让我怎么说呢？

segments.en: Let's just say that at this pace, we will be filing for Chapter 11 in less than three months.
segments.zh: 假设以这个速度，我们将在不到三个月的时间内申请第 11 章。

segments.en: What?
segments.zh: 什么？

segments.en: Jeez, how could this have happened?
segments.zh: 天哪，这怎么会发生？

segments.en: So what's the bad news?
segments.zh: 那么坏消息是什么？

segments.en: Oh, that's the really bad news.
segments.zh: 哦，这真是个坏消息。

segments.en: Our suppliers suffered QC problems and well, half of our production is faulty.
segments.zh: 我们的供应商遇到了 QC 问题，而且我们的一半生产有问题。

segments.en: We're going to have to recall all items sold in the last quarter and the worst part, we're going to have to shoulder this cost.
segments.zh: 上季度卖出的所有产品都得召回，更糟的是费用还得由我们承担。

segments.en: Are you joking?
segments.zh: 你在开玩笑吗？

segments.en: Get the supplier on the line now.
segments.zh: 立刻接通供应商的电话。

segments.en: They have to assume the cost of this mess.
segments.zh: 这烂摊子的费用该由他们出。

segments.en: We tried that, sir.
segments.zh: 我们试过了，先生。

segments.en: The factory has gone under and the owner apparently has fled the country.
segments.zh: 那家工厂已经倒闭，老板似乎也逃到国外去了。

segments.en: We're doomed.
segments.zh: 我们注定要失败。

segments.en: There's some really good news though.
segments.zh: 不过有一些非常好的消息。

segments.en: Really?
segments.zh: 真的吗？

segments.en: What?
segments.zh: 什么？

segments.en: I got offered a new job.
segments.zh: 我找到一份新工作。

segments.en: All right, great.
segments.zh: 好，太好了。

segments.en: So this topic of filing for Chapter 11 is actually very recent, very common now because recently one of the biggest companies filed for Chapter 11 in the US.
segments.zh: 所以第 11 章的这个主题实际上是最近的，现在很常见，因为最近在美国申请第 11 章的最大公司之一。

segments.en: Yeah, that's right.
segments.zh: 对，没错。

segments.en: But I often get confused by the phrase to file for Chapter 11 versus to file for Chapter 13.
segments.zh: 但我经常对第 11 章提交的短语感到困惑，而不是提交第 13 章。

segments.en: All right, so in the United States, the bankruptcy law has different chapters or different sections, right?
segments.zh: 好吧，所以在美国，破产法有不同的章节或不同的部分，对吧？

segments.en: And Chapter 11 is basically for companies that run out of money, that go bankrupt, so they have to declare themselves in bankruptcy and so they file for Chapter 11.
segments.zh: 第 11 章基本上适用于没钱、破产的公司，因此他们必须宣布自己破产，因此他们申请第 11 章。

segments.en: But what about Chapter 13?
segments.zh: 但是第 13 章呢？

segments.en: Chapter 13 is for people.
segments.zh: 第 13 章是给人的。

segments.en: So people who have large debts, maybe with the car company or the telephone company and they can't pay, they file for Chapter 13.
segments.zh: 所以那些负债累累的人，可能是在汽车公司或电话公司，他们无法付款，他们申请了第 13 章。

segments.en: They say, hey, I don't have money, I can't pay.
segments.zh: 他们说，嘿，我没有钱，我付不起。

segments.en: So I guess here it's kind of a metaphor again.
segments.zh: 所以我想这里又是一个隐喻。

segments.en: This phrase to file for Chapter 11 or Chapter 13 meaning bankruptcy.
segments.zh: 该短语为第 11 章或第 13 章申请破产。

segments.en: And people will say personally that they're filing for Chapter 11.
segments.zh: 人们会亲自说他们正在申请第 11 章。

segments.en: Exactly.
segments.zh: 正是这样。

segments.en: Right, so this is an interesting situation because if you file for bankruptcy in some countries, you can go to jail.
segments.zh: 对，所以这是一个有趣的情况，因为如果你在某些国家申请破产，你可能会进监狱。

segments.en: I read recently about this happening in Dubai actually.
segments.zh: 我最近读到了迪拜发生的这件事。

segments.en: Exactly.
segments.zh: 正是这样。

segments.en: So there is prison for debts.
segments.zh: 所以有债务监狱。

segments.en: In the US, you don't go to prison for debts.
segments.zh: 在美国，你不会因为债务而入狱。

segments.en: But what about in your country's listeners?
segments.zh: 但是在贵国的听众中呢？

segments.en: What happens when you go into debt in your country?
segments.zh: 当你在你的国家负债时会发生什么？

segments.en: Or what happens when a company goes into bankruptcy?
segments.zh: 或者当一家公司破产时会发生什么？

segments.en: Let us know.
segments.zh: 告诉我们吧。

segments.en: Come to our website, EnglishPod.com.
segments.zh: 来我们的网站，englishpod.com。

segments.en: Leave your questions and comments.
segments.zh: 留下您的问题和意见。

segments.en: And of course, Erica and I are always there to help you out.
segments.zh: 当然，埃里卡和我总是在那里帮助你。

segments.en: Thanks for downloading you guys and until next time, goodbye.
segments.zh: 感谢您下载你们，直到下一次，再见。

segments.en: Bye.
segments.zh: 再见。

segments.en: Bye-bye.
segments.zh: 拜拜。
